name: K-Board
summary: Single-port family whose application and bootloader both report as K-Board; bootloader state is distinguished by PID MSB = 1.

notes: K-Board's SysEx preamble parser (MIDI_sysex.c: CORE_SX_PACKET_PREAMBLE, in both K-Board_Firmware and K-Board_Bootloader - same shared lineage) stops reading as soon as the fixed 6-byte preamble is decoded, without regard for the 7-bit/8-bit decode's 7-byte group boundaries. Without a flush after the preamble, the first payload byte of a sendSyxFormattedMessage()-based command can land in the same decode group as the tail of the preamble and get silently dropped when the firmware resets its decode buffer right after dispatching.

Confirmed on hardware: firmware_tester --flush-after-preamble (or --device kboard, which reads this field) is required for SYX_CMD_TEST_MODE/SYX_CMD_BURST_MODE payloads to land correctly; without it the command is silently no-op'd, not rejected. See k-board-firmware's .buddy-project/kboard-perf-test-design.md §10.3 for the full investigation.

Validated on real hardware 2026-08-18 (mimic_hub bring-up, K-Board on a Mimic Hub port): `SendSysEx -p <port> -f 'K-Board Firmware v9.0.1.syx' -fcs 64 -fgd 3000 -cs 512 -cd 150 -pd 3000` completed with zero errors. Same underlying receiver behavior as KBP4 (see kbp4.json's own firmwareUpdateDefaults) - the bootloader's `flashErased` flag causes it to erase the entire application region unconditionally on the first valid firmware packet, blocking further USB service until that finishes (see sendsysex/docs/kmi_fw_update_process.md, 'Flash Layout and Boot Flow'). K-Board's own MTU tolerates a slightly larger first window than KBP4's (64B vs 32B) before the in-flight send itself starts failing mid-transmission.

rebootsToAppOnFinalChunk (2026-08-26): K-Board reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk, so it never answers an identity request in bootloader mode afterwards. Skip the doomed final-chunk handshake and let runAutomaticUpdate's application-port reconnect + version check be the success test (same as softstep.json/boppad.json).

CORRECTION (2026-08-26) to the paragraph below: the earlier 'EOF chunk dropped, device stuck in bootloader' reading was a misdiagnosis rooted in K-Board's application and bootloader sharing the SAME port name ('K-Board' - state is distinguished only by the PID MSB in the identity reply, which the tool already checks). The final-chunk handshake was not confirming the bootloader received the EOF; it was accidentally catching the REBOOTED APPLICATION answering an identity request on that same-named port, once it happened to come up within the postDelayMs (3000ms) window. It 'worked', but by coincidence and only after burning that wait; the real, meaningful test has always been the subsequent application-port reconnect + version-match. With rebootsToAppOnFinalChunk set, that test is now the sole arbiter for the final chunk and the coincidental handshake is gone.

This is the multi-chunk (Hex_to_SysEx-chunked) case, unlike KBP4's single-monolithic-message payloads - K-Board's between-chunk identity-handshake already existed and worked; what was missing/broken was the first and last chunks' reply-wait windows both silently using chunkDelayMs (150ms) instead of the much longer firstGapDelayMs/postDelayMs (3000ms) already being passed - fixed in chunkedSysExTransfer.h the same day (see its inline comments and kmi_fw_update_process.md's own addendum). [See the CORRECTION note above re: what the final-chunk reply-wait was actually observing.]
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode while the device still reports as K-Board.
Preferred current production K-Board firmware payload. Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging.

Adds finalizeTareCapture(): a one-time +25% margin applied to the settled boot-time tare average for key/button/bend-pad sensors, capped at 2/3 of range, to reduce reported key over-sensitivity. Bench-validated on real hardware.

NOT a production release. Performance-test firmware variant (perf_test branch of k-board-firmware) that emits synthetic MIDI/SysEx traffic on command and disables physical key/bend-pad input, used to stress-test mimic_hub with up to 13 simultaneous K-Boards.
Version 9.0.1 is deliberately out of the normal release sequence so it's unmistakable in an ID reply. Select explicitly with --fw-version 9.0.1; never the implicit default.
See k-board-firmware's .buddy-project/kboard-perf-test-design.md for the full design and SYX_CMD_TEST_MODE/SYX_CMD_BURST_MODE command reference.
Bootloader uses the same reported product string as the application; confirm state via PID MSB = 1.
